claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on high-fidelity phonon simulations and targeted inelastic-scattering measurements will predict low lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed model will improve predictive accuracy by about 20–30% over conventional averaging or ab initio methods.
FeCoCrMnNi is a strongly disordered multicomponent alloy representative of the proposed material class.
The target high-entropy alloys are single-phase.
Phonon transport dominates in the target alloys between 300 and 700 K.
The framework will integrate simulated phonon lifetimes, local anharmonicity, and force-constant fluctuations with inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering measurements.
The model is applicable only within 300–700 K when chemical disorder remains random and phase segregation or clustering is absent.
Sufficient high-quality simulation and experimental data are required for the model to be accurate.
Atomic-scale disorder in high-entropy alloys manifests as mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering or attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi.
The disorder-enhanced phonon scattering is anharmonic.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes.
Enhanced phonon scattering lowers lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning model will learn quantitative relationships between disorder parameters and reductions in phonon lifetime.
Resolving phonon-mode distributions and local scattering events will overcome the averaging limitations of traditional predictive methods.
The model's lattice-thermal-conductivity predictions will be within a 20–30% error margin of experiment.
The model will reproduce experimentally measured trends in phonon lifetimes.
Standard ab initio, effective-medium, and empirical models average disorder effects and underpredict localized anharmonic scattering, making their thermal-conductivity predictions less accurate.
Phase separation, non-random chemical ordering, or structural transitions will compromise the model's predictive capability.
The magnitude of the claimed accuracy improvement depends on the quality and quantity of training data and on experimental validation of simulated phonon properties.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis promises a 20–30% improvement in accuracy relative to baseline methods, whereas the predicted outcome specifies an absolute 20–30% error relative to experiment. These are different performance metrics and are not made mutually consistent.

The predicted outcome requires only reproduction of trends in phonon lifetimes, but the falsification rule also applies a 20–30% numerical-deviation threshold to phonon lifetimes. That quantitative lifetime-accuracy prediction was not stated in the predicted outcome.
